document_summary: California Apartment Association (secondary source) compliance reminder, dated 2024-09-24, on California fair housing limits on criminal-background screening and 'No Section 8' policies.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council regulations)
rules.requirement: Landlords may check criminal history only within strict fair housing limits on what is sought, how it is considered, and what action is taken. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record and policies that consider arrests without convictions are prohibited.
rules.key_value: Ban on blanket criminal-record exclusions and on considering arrests without convictions
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing decisions by landlords in California using criminal history information.
rules.interaction: Builds on HUD 2016 disparate-impact guidance; local ordinances may add further limits.
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 2, § 12265 (Civil Rights Council regulations, eff. 2020-01-01)
rules.quoted_span: Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal record are prohibited, as are policies that consider arrests without convictions.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source summary; regulation section number not given in the document, supplied from knowledge. Effective date from text: regulations 'took effect Jan. 1, 2020'.}

rules.title: Source of income protection: 'No Section 8' policies prohibited (SB 329)
rules.requirement: State law treats government housing subsidies such as Section 8 as 'source of income' under FEHA, so landlords may not refuse to participate in such programs.
rules.key_value: Ban on refusing Section 8 / government housing subsidy participation
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords subject to FEHA; applies to government housing subsidy programs such as the Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher program.
rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (as amended by SB 329 (2019))
rules.quoted_span: This change meant that, as of Jan. 1, 2020, state law prohibits landlords from refusing to participate in such programs.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source. Document says SB 329 was adopted in 2019; exact adoption date not stated. Effective date from 'as of Jan. 1, 2020'.

rules.title: Credit history use for subsidy holders (SB 267)
rules.requirement: Owners may not use a subsidy-holding applicant's credit history in the application process without offering the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.key_value: Must offer alternative evidence of ability to pay before relying on credit history for applicants with a government rental subsidy
rules.coverage_conditions: Applicants with a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8.
rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 12955 (as amended by SB 267 (2023))
rules.quoted_span: In addition, last year’s [SB 267 amended FEHA](https://caanet.org/whats-new-in-rental-housing-law-for-2024/) to prohibit rental property owners from using a person’s credit history as part of the application process – if they have a government rental subsidy, such as Section 8 — without offering the applicant the option to provide alternative evidence of a verifiable legal means to pay their portion of the rent.
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source; document says only 'last year's SB 267' and gives no effective date, so effective_date is null.
